The purpose of the master plan focuses
on the following key objectives.
One, to complete a data-driven inventory analysis
and analysis of existing park conditions.
Two, to reflect how residents currently use and envision
the future of Victoria Park.
Three, to establish recommendations
for the protection, stewardship, and development of the park.
and four to develop a short and long-term clear implementation strategy.
The Victoria Park Master Plan is composed of three phases.
Phase one, inventory, data collection and analysis.
Phase two, engage in envisioning.
And phase three, the master plan development.
Phase one highlights our quantitative, data-driven approach
to the master plan, which included a thorough inventory
of all existing parks infrastructure.
Our consultant noted areas of focus
as part of the assessment, which included improvements
of the pedestrian pathway network, lighting gaps,
repairs to site furnishings, consistent signage,
and playground area upgrades.
Within phase one as well, we deployed 15 sensor stations
across the park in partnership with the Innovation Lab.
This overview shows an extraction of data from September of last year that indicated
4.6 million visitors to the park in a 12-month period, clearly a well-used space.
And the analysis of this year-over-year baseline data set will be appended to the master plan
and will assist in future strategic and policy work.
This phase for phase two engagement is focused on really listening both internally to staff
perspectives as well as the valuable feedback we received from the public.
We partnered with consultants on this phase as well to build out and facilitate engagement
as well as produce an engagement summary report.
Key themes that emerged from this report included accessibility, safety, connectivity, naturalization
and programming.
For recommendations, this work resulted in 32 final recommendations across capital,
strategic and policy categories, with strong alignment between identified needs and lifecycle
investments.
Implementation for the near term, 2026 to 2028, we focused on six funded capital priorities,
including upgrading the picnic shelter, electrical servicing, active play zone improvements,
basketball courts, trails, and continued data collection.
These six projects fall within the currently funded scope of the implementation budget.
We currently have $2.3 million in the Victoria Park capital budget.
